_comment: Preguntas ORIGINALES tipo NIE del capítulo 1.11. No son preguntas reales del examen. Comprueba con tu edición 2027.

questions.scenario: Under the CPIA Code of Practice, which lines of enquiry must the officer in charge ensure are pursued?
options: All reasonable lines of enquiry, whether they point towards or away from the suspect
Only those pointing towards the suspect
Only those requested by the CPS
Only those requested by the defence

questions.scenario: Which role examines material, creates the schedules and reveals material to the prosecutor?
Who decides what material is disclosed to the defence?
explanations: The police reveal to the prosecutor.

questions.scenario: What is 'relevant material' under the CPIA Code?
options: Material that appears to have some bearing on any offence under investigation, any person investigated, or surrounding circumstances

questions.scenario: A witness's first description of the robber is very different from the suspect. What should happen?
options: Keep it only in a notebook without scheduling
Record, retain and schedule it; it is likely to meet the disclosure test
Give it to the defence directly

questions.scenario: Which schedule lists non-sensitive unused material?
Details of a CHIS (informant) would normally be listed on…
What is the disclosure test in s. 3 CPIA 1996?
options: Material the prosecution will rely on
Material which might reasonably be considered capable of undermining the prosecution case or assisting the accused's case

questions.scenario: In the Crown Court, is a defence statement compulsory?
options: Only if the defendant is represented

questions.scenario: In the magistrates' court, a defence statement is…
After disclosure, the prosecutor must…
options: keep disclosure under review (continuing duty, s. 7A)
only review if the judge asks

questions.scenario: Sensitive material meets the disclosure test. Can the prosecution simply withhold it?
options: Only with a court ruling on public interest immunity (PII)

questions.scenario: If the court orders disclosure of sensitive material the prosecution wants to protect, what may happen?
options: The prosecution may have to discontinue the case

questions.scenario: A shop's CCTV doesn't show the suspect at all. Is it relevant material?
options: Yes – it may point away from the suspect; record, retain and schedule
Only if it shows the crime

questions.scenario: Following conviction, how long must relevant material generally be retained (⚠ check)?
options: Until release from custody or 6 months from conviction, whichever is later

questions.scenario: A schedule describes items as 'miscellaneous papers'. Is this acceptable?
options: No – descriptions must be clear and detailed enough for the prosecutor

questions.scenario: Which form does the disclosure officer use to draw the prosecutor's attention to material that might meet the test?
Previous convictions of a key prosecution witness are…
options: potentially capable of undermining the prosecution case and should be considered for disclosure

questions.scenario: Which Act governs disclosure in criminal investigations?
Can the defence apply to the court for specific disclosure after serving a defence statement?
Who must record and retain relevant material?
A victim's phone may contain messages that undermine her account. What is the correct approach?
options: Consider it as a reasonable line of enquiry, proportionate and respecting privacy (⚠ guidelines)
Ask the defence to do it

questions.scenario: Draft versions of a witness statement that differ from the final version should be…
Which statement about the OIC is correct?
options: The OIC can never be the disclosure officer
The OIC directs the investigation and ensures reasonable lines of enquiry are pursued; roles may be combined in small cases
The OIC is always a superintendent
